_what: The census of every candidate the record has decided against the standing position since Session 26. Hand-built, signed. Population A (development set) was read before the pre-registration and generated the hypothesis; Population B (held-out) was extracted after it, under the rule fixed in PREDICTIONS.md §3. Every 'quote' must be found byte-for-byte in its 'source' — extract.py checks that in both directions and fails loudly.
_sentence: Error is a special case of the epistemic thing — a difference onto which an observer has already imposed a norm.

_verdict_vocabulary.entered-the-sentence: the words of the standing sentence changed
_verdict_vocabulary.entered-the-reading: a word already in the sentence was given a fixed reading, the words unchanged
_verdict_vocabulary.outside: refused, killed, relocated or parked beside the sentence

_signed: The 'minimal_admission_form' of each row is my judgement: the shortest wording of the standing sentence that would carry the claim if it were promoted. The tokenising and the comparison against the sentence's word list are the machine's. The split is stated in PREDICTIONS.md §3.

candidates.quote: Error is a difference between two apparatuses, one of which has been elected the norm.
candidates.minimal_admission_form: Error is a difference between two apparatuses, one of which has been elected the norm.
candidates.note: The candidate amendment as first written. Its own author declined it the same night: 'I am not promoting it. One night on one mechanism in one domain is not enough.'

candidates.quote: Error is a difference between two apparatuses, one of which has been *instituted* as the norm.
candidates.minimal_admission_form: Error is a difference between two apparatuses, one of which has been instituted as the norm.
candidates.note: One word repaired after the euro statute: 'elected' carries a suggestion the case refutes — that the electors will live under the result.

candidates.quote: Error is a difference measured across a cut that has been fixed.
candidates.verdict_word: promoted; 'the first movement of the position since Session 26', in its own night's words
candidates.minimal_admission_form: Error is a difference measured across a cut that has been fixed.
candidates.contested: This row decides P1, so how it is scored matters more than any other judgement in the census, and the two readings are both in the record. The WORK says 'So the amendment is promoted in this form' — the amendment, which is the candidate slot and not the centre. The JOURNAL's state-of-the-line says the amendment is 'withdrawn in its old wording and promoted in a new one — the first movement of the position since Session 26.' I score it by the journal, i.e. against my own hypothesis, because scoring it by the work is scoring it in the direction that saves the hypothesis, and this line killed a candidate at S51 for exactly that manoeuvre. Under the other reading P1 wins; it is recorded here so a reader can score it either way.
candidates.note: The one wording in this record a night promoted, and the record then never used it again: zero occurrences after 2026-08-12 in 452 files. Session 51 killed 'the candidate amendment written at S45, repaired at S46, tested at S47, S48 and S49' — a list that does not name S50, the night that changed its wording — and quoted B2's wording, which S50 had already withdrawn.

candidates.quote: A norm is corrigible where nothing holds a reference to it and incorrigible where something does.
candidates.verdict_word: promoted with B3, explicitly not evidenced, killed with it
candidates.minimal_admission_form: A norm is corrigible where nothing holds a reference to it and incorrigible where something does.
candidates.note: Its own night wrote 'tonight is not evidence for the second line' and recorded the four fits available to it as retro-fits, deliberately not counted.

candidates.quote: Error is a difference between two apparatuses, one of which has been **instituted** as the norm.
candidates.minimal_admission_form: Error is a difference between two apparatuses, one of which has been instituted as the norm.
candidates.note: Killed for a reason that has nothing to do with its words: it survived five tests and could not lose. 'A sentence that absorbs its own counter-example forbids nothing.'

candidates.quote: whether a *material* limit on what can be recorded (676 strings) belongs inside a position
candidates.minimal_admission_form: Error is a difference onto which an observer has already imposed a norm, where a material limit supplied the occasion for judgement.
candidates.note: Session 56's question, answered against its own framing: 'Scarcity manufactures the occasions for judgement. It supplies none of the judgement.'

candidates.quote: In institutional cases, the "observer" of the standing position is not a judge who stands
candidates.minimal_admission_form: Error is a special case of the epistemic thing — a difference onto which an observer has already imposed a norm.
candidates.note: The observer as installed base: it holds the norm in place by inertia rather than by decision, and where large enough rewrites the norm's own category for itself. The note says in as many words: 'The centre does not move.'

candidates.quote: The observer-side term of the standing position
candidates.minimal_admission_form: Error and failure are two names an observer gives one difference onto which it has already imposed a norm.
candidates.note: Two species — a present wrong value, and an expected value absent — and the sign that separates them is itself observer-imposed. The reading entered; the word 'failure' did not enter the sentence. Compare A7: the same manoeuvre, nineteen sessions apart, and neither note cites the other.

candidates.note: EXCLUDED from the lexical test by the extraction rule: a candidate for the working title is not a candidate for the sentence. Recorded here so the exclusion is visible rather than silent.

candidates.minimal_admission_form: Error is a difference onto which one or more observers, who need not agree, have already imposed a norm.
candidates.note: Refused on the ground that the sentence entails it in one step. The measurement — 840 review states, 9 corrections against a green test — was kept in the record instead.

candidates.minimal_admission_form: Error is a special case of the epistemic thing — a difference onto which an observer has already imposed a norm.
candidates.note: The one promotion in the whole series, and it added nothing: it recovered a word that had been read as ordinary English for forty-five sessions. 'Session 26 said error names where the observer stands. Tonight adds: stands has a tense.'

candidates.minimal_admission_form: Error is a difference onto which an observer has imposed a norm born at the breakdown the norm now governs.
candidates.note: Session 60's genesis candidate. S71 removed its exclusive clause ('not about time') and relocated the rest: a claim about genesis that had annexed a word whose main work is temporal. Satellite 1 of Session 84's four.

candidates.minimal_admission_form: Error is a difference onto which an observer has already imposed a norm published by some party.

candidates.minimal_admission_form: Error is a special case of the epistemic thing — a difference onto which an observer has already imposed a norm.
candidates.note: Five relations of a norm to a difference — declared, attached, published, transmitted, acted on — separated in one object, and the verb assigned to exactly one of them.
